title: Promise
body:
An object representing a value that isn't available yet — the result of work happening somewhere other than the current line of code. [[Fetch]] returns one immediately, long before any response has arrived.

**Promise states:**
- `pending` — the work hasn't finished
- `fulfilled` — it finished, and there's a value
- `rejected` — it failed, and there's an error

**Promise methods:**
- `then(fn)` — register a function to run when it fulfils; returns another promise, which is why they chain
- `catch(fn)` — register a function to run if it rejects
- `finally(fn)` — run either way

Because `then` returns a promise, `fetch(url).then(r => r.json()).then(data => ...)` works: each link hands the next one its result. `await` is syntax over exactly this machinery — see [[Async Functions]]. The reason a promise's callback runs "later" rather than blocking is the [[Event Loop]]. See [[Asynchronous JS]] and [[Parallel Fetches]].
